q1_issues.issue: The falling feathers are given Theme, but an intransitive fall driven by gravity is the non-volitional natural-process case the thematic-role section assigns Patient (its own example is 'rain fell').

notes: The instruction set pulls two ways here — 'un-powered relocation ... drifting or dropped things' assigns Theme while 'a mass moved by gravity (rain fell)' assigns Patient — and I read the more specific gravity carve-out as governing a physical fall. Everything else matches: indefinite 'a sky-cat' routes 'when' to the occurrence rule, the bare-plural subject 'feathers' gets a per-occurrence Skolem group, 'the base of the cliff' takes PartOf as a relational-noun genitive, and 'to' takes Goal.
